difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y quasi-finite and separated between spaces over S with Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated, there is a factorization X -> T -> Y with j a quasi-compact open immersion and pi finite — Zariski's Main Theorem in the chapter's spaces form. The retained proof is complete: start from the quasi-affine factorization X -> Y' -> Y (chapter lemma quasi-finite-separated-quasi-affine, card L16060-era family), write the integral algebra nu_*O_{Y'} as a directed colimit of finite subalgebras (Limits of Spaces, lemma integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite) so Y' = lim T_i with T_i finite over Y; descend the open subspace f'(X) to some quasi-compact open U_i subset T_i (lemma descend-opens); realize X as the limit of the pulled-back U_{i'} (lemma directed-inverse-system-has-limit); promote X -> U_{i'} to a closed immersion at a finite stage (lemma finite-type-eventually-closed), making X -> T_{i'} an immersion; the chapter's factor-the-other-way lemma splits it as open immersion X -> T followed by closed immersion T -> T_{i'}, and the composite T -> Y is finite. Retained author proof at lines 7770-7803.
